channel.title: Riddim Yard
channel.description:
Riddim Yard is the home of foundation Jamaican music: Ska, Rocksteady, Deejay, Dub, Roots & Dancehall 
 
email: rickhowe@riddimyard.com.au

item.title: Roberto Sánchez reloads with more Lone Ark exclusives
item.description:
More exclusive pre-release vinyl straight from Roberto Sánchez's Lone Ark Studio in Spain. A fixture at the top of Riddim Yard's producer rankings for many years, Roberto returns with a heavyweight new 45 from Milton Henry - the Black Ark and Wackies veteran - titled Rastafari Can Not Die. Plus fresh 12" and 7" releases from Spanish roots outfit Irieginal Roots.

Also in the mix, new dancehall heat from rising artist Skari with Dancehall Style, alongside the latest from Jahvillani, a fresh gun tune in a modern dancehall style.

And from France, Stand High Patrol link up with UK singer Joe Yorke, bringing his trademark truesetto style and bass-heavy sound system vibrations.
item.author: Rick Howe

item.title: RIP Stranger Cole
item.description:
Paying tribute to our dear friend Stranger Cole. One of the pioneering voices of the ska and rocksteady eras, who continued into the reggae era with a deep catalogue of quality music. Riddim Yard was lucky enough to host Stranger Cole twice on the program over the years. Wilburn Theodore Cole lived his life to fullest, bringing joy to everyone he met. RIP to a true musical legend.

Also on the program, brand new up to the times dancehall from wurl boss Vybz Kartel from his 19th studio album God & Time produced by TJ Records.
item.author: Rick Howe

item.title: Aza Lineage rebels with King Jammy
item.description:
This week on Riddim Yard: One of Jamaica's rising stars, Aza Lineage, teams up with veteran producer King Jammy for the new album Rebel Daawta. Available as a ten-track vinyl edition and an expanded seventeen-track digital release, the set showcases Aza's lyrical skill and vocal versatility across a selection of heavyweight King Jammy productions. From soundsystem-ready anthems and rub-a-dub scorchers to conscious roots reggae, Rebel Daawta is a powerful meeting of emerging talent and one of reggae's most enduring producers.

Also featured is brand new dancehall from Jahvillani ahead of its July 4 release, bringing the kind of up-to-the-times energy that's kept him at the forefront of modern Jamaican music.

Plus, a rare slice of digital dub from Augustus Pablo. A true pioneer whose melodica-driven sound helped redefine reggae and dub, Pablo remains one of the most loved artists on Riddim Yard, with his recordings continuing to inspire generations of producers, musicians and sound system operators.
item.author: Rick Howe

item.title: Lord Watch Over Our Shoulders
item.description:
This week on Riddim Yard: Dennis Brown's classic 1976 album Deep Down celebrates its 50th anniversary. Produced by Winston 'Niney The Observer' Holness, it's one of the Crown Prince's finest roots recordings and a landmark release from one of reggae's greatest singer-producer partnerships.

Also this week, VP continues its digital Garnet Silk reissue series with Lord Watch Over Our Shoulders, one of the late singer's defining recordings, alongside Barrington Levy's True Love - the 1983 Georg Phang production on the classic Swing Easy riddim, finally receiving its first-ever digital release in its full discomix form.

And for the sound system faithful, King Jammy unleashes a devastating collection of exclusive dub plates once used to crush rivals in clashes around the world. Featuring heavyweight cuts from Buju Banton, Bounty Killer, Wayne Wonder, Culture, Garnet Silk, Frankie Paul, Al Campbell and more, it's pure dancehall pressure from one of Riddim Yard's all-time favourite producers.
item.author: Rick Howe

item.title: Too Too Bad
item.description:
Riddim Yard's favourite current artist Lila Iké opens the show with 'What It Feels Like', her outstanding cut on Protoje's Feel It Riddim. Following her GRAMMY-nominated album Treasure Self Love - Riddim Yard's album of the year in 2025 - it's another superb release from one of Jamaica's most compelling voices.

French sound system champions Roll & Record reunite with Pili Boyo on the uplifting new 7" 'One By One', a heavyweight roots anthem produced by William Spring. Plus Roberto Sánchez and The 18th Parallel return via Fruits Records with 'Morning Blessing', the second taste of the forthcoming Showcase Vol. 2 album - a thunderous steppers workout recorded to 2-inch tape in Switzerland and Spain that celebrates gratitude and life's blessings.

And one of dancehall's greatest ever voices is back where he belongs. Buju Banton returns to VP Records after 23 years with his thirteenth studio album Too Too Bad, delivering the uncompromising hardcore dancehall sound that made 'The Gargamel' a legend. Four tracks from the new album feature in this week's edition.
item.author: Rick Howe
